label: Post-disturbance weather sequence
definition: Order and wetness of the years that follow a disturbance (wet vs dry years, drought timing), including whether effects are observed in low- or high-snow years.
why_it_matters: The same disturbance can raise or lower ET and yield depending on the years that follow; short observation windows may not generalize.
model_representation_needed: Multi-year forcing and experiments that vary disturbance timing relative to climate; not a model-coverage question.

label: Background aridity / water vs energy limitation
definition: Whether pre-disturbance ET was mainly water- or energy-limited; annual precipitation regime.
why_it_matters: Vegetation change tends to dominate yield response in dry regions and interannual climate in wetter ones; simple precipitation thresholds do not predict decreases.
model_representation_needed: Water-stress limitation of transpiration and soil evaporation.

label: Rain-snow regime
definition: Fraction of precipitation falling as snow, and shifts toward rain.
why_it_matters: Changes which canopy-snow processes matter; reported decreases cluster in regions expected to lose snow.

label: Disturbance type and severity
definition: Stand-replacing (clearcut, high-severity fire) vs partial removal (insects, drought, thinning, low-severity fire), and removal intensity.
why_it_matters: Partial disturbances more often give no change or decreases in yield; response scales nonlinearly with intensity.
model_representation_needed: Disturbance/mortality that can remove part of the stand, with survivors.

label: Disturbance extent and spatial position
definition: Fraction of watershed affected, riparian vs upslope position, patchiness and severity mosaic.
why_it_matters: Area-affected rules of thumb mask density variation; water released upslope may be used downslope rather than reaching the stream.
model_representation_needed: Spatially distributed disturbance with lateral water redistribution.

label: Recovery rate and growth release
definition: Speed of regrowth and of residual-plant growth after disturbance, including overshoot above pre-disturbance leaf area.
why_it_matters: Rapid regrowth can erase or reverse yield gains within about a decade; growth pulses can raise later drought stress.
model_representation_needed: Prognostic vegetation (dynamic LAI/biomass) rather than prescribed or static post-disturbance cover.

label: Understory and residual vegetation water use
definition: Transpiration by surviving trees, advance regeneration, shrubs and herbs after overstory loss.
why_it_matters: Can offset or exceed overstory ET loss, producing unchanged or reduced yield.
model_representation_needed: Separate understory canopy layer with its own water and energy fluxes.

label: Species or vegetation-type change
definition: Shift in dominant functional type during recovery (e.g., conifer forest to shrubland).
why_it_matters: Dense, high-LAI replacement vegetation can use more water than the forest it replaced.
model_representation_needed: Community composition / PFT change during recovery.

label: Fine-scale canopy structure and density
definition: Gap size, residual stem density and canopy cover within disturbed stands, not just area disturbed.
why_it_matters: Snow retention and subcanopy radiation respond nonlinearly to density; the snow-retention optimum differs between warm and cold winters.
model_representation_needed: Canopy radiative transfer, snow interception, sub-grid gaps.
notes: Includes canopy_structure example row in process_coverage.csv as a likely match.

label: Radiation exposure (latitude, aspect, elevation)
definition: Net radiation reaching the surface as set by sun angle and terrain.
why_it_matters: Yield and SWE decreases concentrate where radiation is high; aspect can outweigh vegetation effects on snow.
model_representation_needed: Topographic correction of shortwave and longwave radiation.

label: Subcanopy evaporation and snowpack sublimation
definition: Soil evaporation and ground-snow sublimation that increase when the canopy opens.
why_it_matters: Can offset reduced transpiration and canopy interception losses.
model_representation_needed: Soil evaporation and snowpack sublimation driven by subcanopy radiation and turbulence.

label: Snow-surface albedo (litter and char)
definition: Needles, bark and charred debris darkening the snow surface after insects or fire.
why_it_matters: Speeds ablation, so SWE can decline even when interception decreases.
model_representation_needed: Snow albedo that responds to litter/debris deposition.

label: Snowmelt synchrony across the watershed
definition: Whether disturbance aligns or spreads melt timing across elevations and aspects.
why_it_matters: Controls whether peak flows rise, fall or shift in timing.

label: Plant-accessible water storage capacity
definition: Water that roots can reach and use, held in soil, saprolite and fractured bedrock.
why_it_matters: Determines whether water released by disturbance relieves stress of survivors, is transpired, or drains.
model_representation_needed: Rooting-zone storage capacity (rooting depth, field capacity, wilting point).

label: Root water sharing among neighbors
definition: Whether remaining plants can access water previously used by removed plants (belowground neighborhood).
why_it_matters: Sets how quickly survivors capture released water and can flip the sign of the ET change.
model_representation_needed: Sub-grid root access to shared vs local storage; individual/cohort vs bulk-stand representation.

label: Deeper storage and flowpaths
definition: Depth to bedrock, deep storage and lateral flowpaths that route released water to streams or downslope vegetation.
why_it_matters: Determines whether water not used on site reaches streamflow.

label: Post-fire soil changes
definition: Water repellency and altered infiltration after fire.
why_it_matters: Shifts partitioning toward overland flow and can change peak flows.
model_representation_needed: Fire effects on infiltration and surface runoff.
